sources.title: How to Use Amazon’s Narrative Process to Improve Your Writing, Communications and Decision-making
sources.author: Richard Howard, AWS Startup Business Development
sources.accessScope: Introduction, narrative definition, starting guidance, and beginning of fictional example read.
sources.rights: Public explanatory article; no permissive license verified. Original summary only; fictional example not copied.

rules.intent: Preserve facts, numbers, units, negation, conditions, exceptions, uncertainty, quotations, citations, and code at every level.
rules.rationale: Shared project meaning-preservation requirement; style never authorizes factual change.

rules.intent: Explain the purpose, reader decision, and essential background for reviewers outside the immediate team.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.

rules.intent: Connect important claims and proposed actions to evidence while distinguishing assumptions and uncertainty.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: If evidence is missing, name the gap instead of fabricating support.

rules.intent: Develop the argument in connected prose with headings and supporting tables only where useful.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: A table, figure, or list may be clearer for genuinely parallel information.

rules.intent: Use a six-page main-body ceiling only with a specified and inspected rendered layout; put supporting detail in appendices without hiding decision-critical limits. For an excerpt with its own word limit, deliver that excerpt within its limit and omit page-count commentary.
rules.rationale: Original operational guidance adapted from the identified source scope.
exceptions: When six physical pages were requested but the output cannot be paginated, qualify the page check outside the narrative.
An opening, excerpt or fixed word budget follows the requested length.
